To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed implicit negative sub-catergorization and sink diversion are two effective methods to improve the performance of proposal classification for object detection.

(1) we propose to divide “background” category into multiple implicit categories, which can be used to improve the proposal classification stage, (2) we propose to use sink diversion to lift performance, (3) we propose to apply dilated convolution to extract context information, (4) our proposed method can be easily integrated into existing object detection methods

the “background class” is generally very diverse, and thus it should be handled as multiple sub-categories; the ground truth class has low-value probability for certain images, and thus it is necessary to divert the probability of wrong classes to a “sink” when necessary; dilated convolution can be used for efficient and valuable feature representation.
